description: Quantum-safe and hybrid encryption for .NET. Post-quantum (ML-KEM, ML-DSA) plus AES-256-GCM, RSA-4096, password hashing and large-file streaming in one simple API — the same encryption across .NET, Android, Swift and JavaScript. Implements the NIST FIPS 203/204/205 algorithms and a BSI-conformant profile.
releaseNotes:
v1.0.10.0 - Large-file streaming encryption (SaQura Stream v1 / SQS1)
New streaming encryption API for large files (videos, backups, 10 GB+
uploads) in the SaQura namespace:
- Encrypts in fixed segments at constant memory (~2x segment size,
  default 1 MiB) regardless of file size - no ~2 GB byte[] ceiling.
  New entry points: Stream.EncryptStreamAsync / DecryptStreamAsync,
  StreamingExtensions.EncryptFileAsync / DecryptFileAsync,
  Stream.ReadStreamInfoAsync, StreamingExtensions.CountCompleteSegments.
- Two AEAD cipher suites, chosen automatically from the file header:
  StreamCipherSuite.AesGcm (FIPS-eligible) and ChaCha20Poly1305
  (RFC 8439, faster on mobile CPUs without AES acceleration).
- Post-quantum streaming envelope (StreamingEnvelopeExtensions, Pro
  tier): a random file key streams the data and is wrapped once with a
  SaQura Quantum key pair (e.g. Gen8 / FIPS 203). EnvelopeKeyPlacement
  .Sidecar (separate .saqkey file - enables crypto-shredding) or
  .Embedded. Streaming is Standard-tier+; the envelope is Pro-tier+.
- New format uses its own SQS1 magic - fully additive and backward-
  compatible; no existing method or wire format changed.
- SQS1 streams are byte-identical across the .NET, Kotlin and Swift
  SaQura libraries (both cipher suites, both envelope placements).
Security:
- Hardened license enforcement and free-tier provenance; the compile-
  time debug path is inert in Release builds. No public API change.
Unchanged:
- AES, RSA, Quantum Gen1-Gen8, ML-DSA / SLH-DSA APIs and wire formats.

v1.0.9.0 - NIST Post-Quantum FIPS: ML-KEM Hybrid (Gen8) + ML-DSA + SLH-DSA Signatures
New post-quantum capabilities (Pro tier and above):
- Generation 8 hybrid key encapsulation: X25519 combined with ML-KEM
  (FIPS 203) for defense-in-depth quantum-safe encryption. The two
  shared secrets are combined via HKDF-SHA256 before AES-256-GCM.
- ML-DSA digital signatures (FIPS 204) in strengths 44 / 65 / 87.
  Sign and verify over arbitrary messages.
- SLH-DSA digital signatures (FIPS 205, SHA2) in strengths
  128f / 192f / 256f. Stateless hash-based, conservative security.
- Signing requires a Pro (or higher) license; signature verification
  is available to all tiers.
- Wire formats are byte-identical across the .NET, Swift and Kotlin
  SaQura libraries, enabling cross-platform sign/verify and hybrid
  key exchange.
- Additive release: no breaking changes to existing AES, RSA or
  Quantum Gen1-Gen7 APIs.

v1.0.8.0 - Cross-Platform Wire-Format Alignment + Defense-in-Depth + Online Activation Fix
Online license activation fix:
- ApiLicense.ActivateLicenseAsync(licenseKey) now correctly parses the
  license-server's wrapped response { success, errorMessage, license,
  signature } that the previous code path deserialized as a flat
  LicenseInfo (always failed signature verification, fell back to
  "Use license file for offline activation"). Online activation has
  been broken since at least v1.0.0.2; .lic-file activation
  (ActivateLicenseFileAsync / ActivateLicenseFromJsonAsync) was the
  workaround and continues to work unchanged.
- License-server request serialization switched to System.Text.Json
  source-generation. Faster than reflection, AOT-ready, no public-API
  change.

Obfuscation hardening:
- Multi-stage obfuscation pipeline strengthened. Method bodies are no
  longer trivially decompilable to readable IL, and plaintext occurrences
  of sensitive symbols are eliminated (UTF-8 + UTF-16LE verified).
- No public-API or behaviour change for consumers.

Cross-platform interop with Swift + Kotlin SaQura libraries:
- AES-256-GCM byte[] APIs: removed legacy base64 inner-wrap from the
  byte[] encrypt/decrypt path. New wire format [Nonce:12][CT:N][Tag:16]
  is byte-identical to Swift's Data.encryptWithAES + Kotlin's
  AESCryptographyHelper.encrypt(ByteArray, key). String-API path is
  unchanged. (See Migration note.)
- RSA-4096 hybrid encryption: canonical wire format
  [KeyLen:4 LE = 512][EncKey:512][Nonce:12][Tag:16][CT:N] now matches
  the cross-platform Swift + Kotlin output. No behaviour change for
  .NET-only callers; the .NET wire format itself was already canonical.
- PBKDF2-SHA512 password hashes: JSON key names aligned to the long-key
  form (algorithm/version/parameters/createdUtc + inner hashAlgorithm/
  iterations/outputLength/saltLength). createdUtc timestamps emit as
  yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ (no fractional seconds) for cross-platform
  ISO-8601 compatibility. Dual-shape DeserializeDualShape reader still
  verifies legacy short-key hashes from v1.0.0.2..v1.0.7 — existing
  user hashes continue to verify after the lib update.
- Quantum Generation 6 with Medium strength: encrypt path now uses
  the actual encapsulated-secret length (was a stale lookup table
  hardcoded to 9720 bytes, only correct for Standard strength). All
  15 gen×strength combos now round-trip cleanly.

Defense-in-Depth on Quantum API:
- Quantum APIs (EncryptWithQuantumAsync, EncryptWithQuantumToBytesAsync,
  DecryptWithQuantumAsync, Quantum.GenerateKeyPair) now reject null,
  empty, and all-zero byte buffers passed as keys or encapsulated
  secrets. Throws ArgumentException with a clear "caller likely zero-
  wiped the array" message — surfaces consumer bugs that previously
  presented as silent (null, null) tuples downstream.
- Output sanity-net: if an internal helper returns a null or empty
  buffer despite the v1.0.5 typed-exception fix, the wrapping API now
  raises the appropriate QuantumOperationException subtype with an
  InvalidOperationException inner.

AES byte[] migration helper:
- New `byte[].MigrateLegacyAESByteCiphertextAsync(string key)` extension
  recovers original plaintext from pre-1.0.8 stored byte[] AES
  ciphertext (SaQura ≤ 1.0.7 output). In-place upgrade:
      byte[] raw = await old.MigrateLegacyAESByteCiphertextAsync(key);
      byte[] new = await raw.EncryptWithAESAsync(key);  // cross-platform
  Verified against all historical AES byte[] outputs from v1.0.0.2
  through v1.0.7.

Migration:
- AES byte[] data from v1.0.7 or earlier: use the new
  MigrateLegacyAESByteCiphertextAsync helper, then re-encrypt.
  String-API AES data is unaffected.
- RSA hybrid + PBKDF2 + Quantum data round-trips unchanged.

v1.0.6.0 - Security Hardening
- Internal license-gate diagnostics removed from Release builds.
- No behavioural change for licensed customers. If you previously
  relied on undocumented internal diagnostic flags, contact support.

v1.0.5.0 - Diagnostic Exceptions for Quantum Operations
- Quantum key generation, encryption and decryption now raise typed
  exceptions (QuantumOperationException + three subtypes) on failure
  instead of returning silent null/empty values.
- Authentication failures during decryption (wrong key or tampered
  ciphertext) continue to return string.Empty.
- Behavioural change: callers that relied on null-on-failure should
  catch QuantumOperationException (or System.Security.Cryptography
  .CryptographicException, which it inherits from).

v1.0.4.7 - Security Hardening
- Prevents license activation timeout

v1.0.4.4 - iOS Mobile Platform Fix
- Improved mobile platform detection
- Prevents license activation timeout on iOS devices

v1.0.4.2 - Maintenance Release
- Documentation improvements

v1.0.3.2 - Server Rejection Handling
- Background server registration
- Improved error messages from server

v1.0.2.2 - iOS/macOS AES Fix
- Fixed PlatformNotSupportedException on Apple platforms

v1.0.1.0 - Distribution Licenses
- Added Distribution License type for App Store/Play Store apps
- No hardware binding, unlimited activations
